title.narrative: Emergency Protection Services for Prevention and Response to CRSV/GBV Among Returnees, IDPs, and Vulnerable Women and Girls in Amhara Region and contested areas.

description.narrative: The project focuses on the provision of emergency protection services addressing sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) and conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV) among vulnerable populations, especially women and girls among returnees, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and host communities in Amhara and Southern Tigray, Western and North-Western Zones in the contested areas. This initiative seeks to address the urgent need for prevention, response, protection, and rehabilitation services for those affected by violence, especially amid ongoing humanitarian crises and protracted displacement. Through its unique monitoring, reporting, and advocacy functions, OHCHR will support a coordinated, multisectoral approach to reduce risks and mitigate harm against affected individuals, empowering survivors and at-risk individuals to live safely and with dignity.The project will implement a comprehensive CRSV/GBV response package with prevention and risk mitigation measures to support the most vulnerable. Activities will include establishing safe spaces, crisis counselling, medical and psychosocial support, legal assistance, and referral pathways. The project will also build capacity among local organizations and community members, empowering them to identify, respond to, and prevent future cases of violence. In adopting this multifaceted approach, OHCHR-EARO will collaborate with key clusters—WASH, child protection, health, food security, and CCCM—and engage multiple levels of local and international stakeholders, including government entities, NGOs, and community groups. Through these efforts, the project aims to address immediate protection needs and strengthen community resilience, accountability mechanisms, and local capacity to safeguard vulnerable populations, especially women, children, the elderly, persons with disabilities, and those displaced due to conflict and violence.OHCHR’s unique role in the project centers on its mandate and expertise in monitoring, reporting, and advocacy, which will be critical in documenting cases of SGBV, CRSV, and human rights violations, advocating for justice and policy change, and enhancing protection measures for those at risk. Through dedicated monitoring missions, OHCHR will document cases of violence, provide critical data for early warning systems, and work to strengthen referral pathways, enabling timely access to services for those affected. Robust monitoring and reporting will enhance accountability by providing comprehensive data on CRSV/GBV trends, which will be used to guide evidence-based advocacy and improve access to justice. Establishing and bolstering Early Warning Mechanisms is integral to this work, as these systems will help identify specific risks and enable rapid preventive action and timely intervention in response to emerging threats. In collaboration with partners, OHCHR’s role in advocating for justice for survivors and addressing impunity will reinforce long-term protections for human rights, particularly for women and girls who have experienced or are at risk of CRSV/GBV.In collaboration with UNFPA and UN Women, OHCHR will leverage the specialized capacities and strengths of each partner organization. UNFPA’s expertise in delivering sexual and reproductive health services and UN Women’s focus on women’s rights and gender equality will complement OHCHR’s protection, monitoring, and advocacy efforts. This collaboration will ensure that the project takes a holistic approach, addressing not only the immediate needs of survivors and at-risk populations but also building a foundation for sustainable protections and support for vulnerable groups. By working together, the agencies aim to better protect women and girls in the target regions, enhance their access to justice, and promote gender equality in the context of SGBV and CRSV.
